name: Sabtah
overview: Sabtah is a male figure identified in Scripture as a son of Cush. Beyond his paternal lineage, the biblical record does not provide additional details about his tribe, surname, or other distinguishing notes. His mention situates him within the genealogical framework of Genesis 10:7.
namesAndTitles: The name Sabtah appears as a proper name in the biblical text without an explicit meaning or divine origin indicated. It is simply recorded as Sabtah in Genesis 10:7.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Sabtah as a son of Cush, establishing a direct paternal relationship. No other family connections or relationships are documented beyond this.
scriptureSignificance: Sabtah's significance lies in his place within the genealogical line descending from Cush, who is a son of Ham. This genealogy in Genesis 10:7 traces the origins of various peoples, highlighting the diverse nations that emerged after the Flood. Sabtah contributes to the biblical understanding of the spread of humanity and the fulfillment of God's command to multiply and fill the earth.
